summary.headline: KVB posted record FY26 net profit of INR2,500 crores (+29%) and Q4 NIM of 4.25%, but guides FY27 NIM down to 3.75-3.8% and ROA to 1.7-1.8%.
summary.overview: Karur Vysya Bank reported record quarterly net profit of INR725 crores and full-year profit of INR2,500 crores (+29%), with full-year NIM of 3.97% above guidance. Total business grew 15% to INR2,14,420 crores, with advances up 17% to INR98,754 crores and deposits up 13% to INR1,15,666 crores, though advances growth moderated in Q4 by conscious choice. Management flagged a shift toward preserving relationships over margins: FY27 credit growth is guided at 1-2% above industry, NIM at 3.75-3.8%, and ROA at 1.7-1.8%. Asset quality stayed stable with GNPA at 0.75% and a one-time INR163 crore prudential provision taken against geopolitically exposed sectors.

financial_highlights.change: Highest quarterly profit in bank history
Includes INR163 crore one-time prudential provision

financial_highlights.value: INR187 crores (Q4); INR744 crores (FY26, 0.75% of loans)
financial_highlights.change: FY26 includes ~INR200 crore Q2 chunky slippages
Cost of deposits down 13 bps QoQ

financial_highlights.value: INR679 crores (FY26) excluding INR139 crore interest recovery

segments.name: Retail advances
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew 25% YoY and 3% QoQ, driven by mortgages (+56% YoY) and jewel loans (+61% YoY). Housing loans grew only 2%, and BNPL book stands at INR798 crores after a partner management change.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agri book grew 19% YoY (5% QoQ) per the call, with agri jewel loans at 91% of agri and LTV of 55.59%; management also cites 5% growth for the year, which is inconsistent with the 19% figure.

segments.name: Commercial and corporate
segments.commentary: Commercial book grew 11.56% YoY but was flat in Q4; corporate grew 12% YoY, or 20% including credit substitutes (incremental INR969 crores). Growth focused on CRE, capital markets and EPC contractors.

segments.name: Deposits
segments.commentary: CASA grew 12%, adding INR3,290 crores vs INR677 crores last year; savings deposits added INR2,505 crores. Bulk deposits grew 9% YoY vs 44% prior year, and CDs of INR1,773 crores were reduced in March.

guidance_outlook: FY27 credit growth guided at 1-2% above industry growth, versus 18% achieved in FY26 (RAM and corporate mix 18-20%, with ~5% flex).
FY27 NIM guided at 3.75-3.8% (management also cited 3.7-3.8% on the call), with exit-Q4 NIM above 4%; drop expected from retail term deposit repricing from April 2026 and lower advance yields.
FY27 ROA guided at 1.7-1.8%; credit cost guided at below 1%.
GNPA below 1.5%, net NPA below 1%, slippages below 1% of the asset book, cost-to-income below 50%, LCR maintained at 115-120%.

Branch expansion of 50 branches in FY27 (38 regular, 7 lite, 5 to be shortlisted), front-loaded into H1. Investment yield enhancement of 15-20 bps via HTM rebalancing; duration to be kept around 4-4.5 years over the medium term.

Management sees no need to raise capital in FY27; profit ploughback to fund growth. Dividend declared at 130%, subject to shareholder approval, with the payout on a larger base after the 1:5 bonus issued last year.
capex_capacity: Plan to open 50 branches in FY27: 38 regular, 7 lite, and 5 yet to be shortlisted; front-loading into H1 to capture benefit in Q2.
Management says capital is not a constraint: CRAR at 18.76% with Tier 1 dominant and RWA-to-total-assets at 55-58%, with room to take it up to around 65% over time.
Loan-against-mutual-fund IT integration is at final stage, expected launch in H1 FY27; premium credit cards planned in FY27.
Digital: 98% of transactions digital; DLite app rated 4.8 on Google Play and 4.6 on Apple App Store, with 2.5 million monthly active users.
demand_pricing: Retail term deposit rates raised in April 2026; new products at 7.2%, with blended incremental cost seen at 7.2-7.5% as senior citizen deposits are 27-30% of total deposits.

Competition on yields has intensified from private and public sector banks; management said concession pricing has moved ahead and it may have to cut rates to existing and new borrowers to retain accounts.
Corporate lending: management chose to lean into BBB-rated accounts with gating conditions, with the stated aim of lifting RWA density, while acknowledging fierce competition for AAA/AA names.
Gold loans: jewel loans are 30% of the book against an internal cap of 35%; agri gold yields are about 10.75-11%, and management plans to cut pricing toward 9.5-9% to limit growth.
Working capital utilisation fell 2-3% across sectors in Q4, as customers ran down lines amid geopolitical uncertainty; textile is flagged as the most exposed sector.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 NIM guidance versus the FY26 beat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 3.75-3.8% for FY27, citing sticky deposit costs, leakage of existing customers to competitors, and the need to concede yields to retain top line, accepting some NIM compromise.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the competitive pressure on yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said concession pricing has moved and the bank has held rates, but it now must cut to retain good accounts. Retaining accounts is a priority over margins; Q4 yield benefit of 16 bps came from repricing of 25-30% of the book.

qa_highlights.question: What sectors received the INR163 crore prudential provision?
qa_highlights.answer: Textiles, ceramics, fertilisers, chemicals, granite and quartz, plus other sectors with direct or indirect geopolitical exposure; provisioning was set on a portfolio basis after sector reviews.

qa_highlights.question: Will the ECL transition and steady-state credit cost be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is still reviewing the final RBI ECL guidelines and will share clarity later; FY27 credit cost is guided below 1%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 credit growth guided lower than FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the bank chose a prudent, moderated approach in a benign-but-volatile environment to avoid credit cost offsetting yield gains, with capital not the binding constraint.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gold loan LTV and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gold loans are capped at 75% LTV for retail and 80-85% for agri, with margin of 20-40%; loans above 75% LTV are under 1-1.5% of the portfolio.

risks_watch: NIM trajectory: FY27 guided at 3.75-3.8% vs 3.97% in FY26, with the retail deposit repricing impact to be seen in Q1 FY27.
Yield pressure from competition and existing-customer leakage in corporate, MSME and LAP segments.
Geopolitical exposure: INR163 crore prudential buffer on textiles, ceramics, chemicals and others; West Asia conflict impact on input costs and working capital demand.
Gold price risk: jewel loans at 30% of book; management says a 40% gold price fall would not breach LTV buffers.
ECL transition impact on steady-state credit cost is not yet quantified.
Wage revision provision from November 2026 (IBA committee not yet formed) is not yet provided.
Deposit franchise: term deposit renewals of 70-75% in retail; the flow of new deposits may be insufficient, which may push up cost of funds.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the FY26 delivery and record profit, but cautious and defensive on FY27: management openly trades margin for relationships and growth, and gave a moderated outlook while acknowledging volatility. Answers on capital, ECL and the wage provision were non-committal, with several deferred to later updates.
